publicationStmt.p: Working authority file for the Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons. Publication details and licensing will be established for the corpus.

sourceDesc.p: Event records will be compiled from reviewed colophon passages and supporting historical scholarship. Four initial records identify occurrences referenced in the English translation of Colophon 1.

projectDesc.p: This file identifies historical occurrences discussed in the colophons, allowing passages in different colophons and witnesses to refer to the same occurrence. It identifies events, not types of passage or formula categories.

editorialDecl.p: Event identifiers follow the pattern event-000001. Allocate each identifier once and retain it when labels, dates, or identifications are revised. Do not reuse retired identifiers.

Use one event per occurrence inside listEvent. Use eventName for a concise editorial label and note for a description, supporting evidence, or uncertainty. An event record may represent an occurrence known only through a colophon; its existence here does not imply independent historical confirmation.
Event/@type is optional but desired. Use it only when a useful classification emerges from the corpus, documenting its meaning here.

Use event/@type="journey" for identifiable journeys as sub type of event. Record travellers, dates, departure, destination, intermediate stops, and purpose where supported. Distinguish personal travel from manuscript movement.

Normalized dates may be recorded on event: when for an occurrence dated to a specified year or date; from and to for a supported duration; notBefore and notAfter for uncertain temporal bounds. Do not confuse duration with uncertainty. Omit unsupported dates and never infer a precise day from a year-only reference. Explain dating sources, calendar conversions, and disagreements in a note. Original date expressions and their contextual interpretation remain in the edition.

Use optional event/@where to point to an identified place, and placeName/@ref in descriptive notes to name that place. Use persName/@ref for securely identified participants when relevant. Reuse places.xml and persons.xml records instead of defining people or places again here.

The authority record supplies an evidenced identification and concise account. The colophon edition preserves the witness's wording, chronology, perspective, and claims. If accounts disagree, retain the disagreement and explain the basis of identification; do not silently correct the text to match this record.

In the edition, use seg/@type to describe the passage, for example historicalNarrative, and seg/@corresp to link to this file's event record. A historical narrative may remain unlinked when an occurrence cannot be identified.
Use bibl with a reference to bibliography.xml and citedRange for supporting scholarship.

revisionDesc.change: Added four historical-event records matching existing pointers in Colophon 1.

event.note: The capture of Antioch by the Franks. Colophon 1 narrates their arrival, siege, and capture of the city.
The edition retains the colophon's own wording and chronology; this year does not derive from the manuscript's production date of 1099.
Identified in the historical narrative in Colophon 1, folio 279v, English translation.

bibl.note: Insert a supporting bibliography.xml reference and the relevant citedRange for the event's identification and historical dating.

event.eventName: Arrival and defeat of the Muslim army at Antioch
event.note: The arrival of a Muslim army at Antioch and its defeat by the Franks. Colophon 1 describes the army as comprising Turks, Persians, Arabs, and Muslims. The linked narrative includes the encirclement, battle, Frankish victory, and subsequent thanksgiving at the church of Saint Peter.
The normalized historical year 1098, relative intervals stated by the colophon remain part of its narrative account.
Identified in the connected passages of Colophon 1, folio 279v, English translation and folio 280r, English translation. Both passages retain the same event pointer.
The stated army size, group labels, and explanation of victory are reported claims of the colophon, not independently confirmed by this record.

event.note: The capture of Jerusalem by the Franks. Colophon 1 narrates the city's capture and the killing of its opponents.
The edition's note interprets the expression “in the same year” as referring to Armenian era 548 (1099 CE), stated earlier in the colophon.
Identified in the historical narrative in Colophon 1, folio 280r, English translation.

event.note: The execution of Yovhannes, brother of Aharovn, as reported in Colophon 1. The colophon attributes the execution to the Southern nations.
The report occurs in the colophon dated 1099. No independent date of the execution is supplied; no normalized event date is assigned.
The location and more precise identification of those responsible remain unspecified. This occurrence is recorded on the evidence of the colophon.
Reported in Colophon 1, folio 279r, English translation.
